submitted.rationale: Index 22 (Mn 0.223, Sb 0.777) had the highest photocurrent of the three measured points, at 7e-8 A. It beat Mn 0.34 (3e-8 A) and Mn 0.139 (6e-8 A), which points to a peak near Mn about 0.2. That is close to the near-hull MnSb4O12 composition, whose predicted gap of about 2.2 eV is below the 3.22 eV photon energy. The Sb2O3 end has a predicted gap of 3.77 eV, so it would absorb poorly.

rejected.reason: Measured 3e-8 A. MnSb2O6 composition, which is stable, but the photocurrent was lower.
Measured 6e-8 A, slightly below index 22. The photocurrent falls off as Sb increases and absorption drops.

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): MnSb2O6 is on the MACE hull (stable phase at Mn~0.33), so a well-crystallized single-phase film is likely near index 13 (Mn 0.338). MEGNet gap for MnSb2O6 (0.02 eV) is implausible/uninformative; related Sb-rich phases give 2.2-2.5 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so absorption is plausible.

Support, moderately: MnSb4O12 (Mn 0.2) sits only 0.067 eV/atom above the hull. Its predicted gap earlier was 2.19 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy. Index 22 (Mn 0.223) is likely a MnSb2O6 plus Sb-oxide mixture or a metastable Sb-rich phase, and it tests a region distinct from index 13.

Mixed: the Sb2O3 end member has a predicted gap of 3.77 eV, above the 3.22 eV photon energy, so pure Sb oxide would absorb poorly. Some Mn is needed for absorption. The measured photocurrent rose from Mn 0.34 to Mn 0.22, so I am extrapolating moderately to Mn 0.139 (index 28). That balances the trend against the risk of losing absorption toward the Sb end.
